title: Keep partial bytes in the queue when closing a byte stream
body: When a readable byte stream is closed while the first pending pull-into descriptor holds only part of an element, `ReadableByteStreamControllerClose` used to error the stream and throw. This isn't great for two reasons: * Both "close a ReadableStream" and `ReadableByteStreamTee` use `!`, so `ReadableByteStreamControllerClose` wasn't even *allowed* to throw. * Fundamentally, this is not a valid reason to error the stream: it's not the fault of the underlying byte source that the BYOB reader is trying to do a multi-byte read when the source is out of bytes and wants to close the stream. Instead, the stream now becomes close-requested. When the underlying byte source responds to the pending BYOB request, the incomplete element is put back into the queue, and the pending read-into requests are handled as if they were made after `close()`: each one is fulfilled with as many whole elements as are available, or fails with a `TypeError` if not even one element is available. The stream becomes closed once the queue is drained. Similarly, a `read(view)` on a close-requested stream whose queue cannot reach the minimum fill no longer errors the stream. Fixes #1387.
